mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals restrictive monetary policy that increases equity discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of historical instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 4.5% indicates a deteriorating labor market, reducing consumer spending and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in retail sales and housing starts (RSAFS < 350000 and HOUST < 1800) signal broad consumer demand weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS < 350000 and HOUST < 1800.
